title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 4th draft ('mouture') of the 1986 Analysis situs chapter. Grothendieck is building a purely combinatorial axiomatics for tame 'figures', meaning stratified subsets of a space. On the previous page he set up the 'atlas' point of view: a set \mathcal F of figures with relations ≤, ≪, a compatibility relation (symbol ≍ crossed out, transcribed ≭ below), and |o|. At1 says bounded families have a Sup and \mathcal F has a least element. Elementary figures are completely join-irreducible elements (X = Sup F_i ⇒ X = F_i for some i). M is the set of elementary figures, and \tilde F = {X ∈ M | X ≤ F}. At2 says the elementary figures are join-dense and order-determining: F ≤ G iff \tilde F ⊂ \tilde G, i.e. every figure is the Sup of its strata.

This page completes the list.
- Def: F ≭ G ('compatible') iff {F,G} is bounded above, equivalently F ∨ G exists.
- At3: compatibility is determined by elementary pieces. F ≭ G iff X ≭ Y for all X ∈ \tilde F and Y ∈ \tilde G. The NB notes that the ⇒ direction is already known.
- At4: the relation ≪ (an incidence / 'lies in the closure-boundary of' type relation) on figures is induced from elementary ones. F ≪ G iff every X ∈ \tilde F satisfies X ≪ Y for some Y ∈ \tilde G.
- At5a: |o| is really a relation on M; it only holds between elementary figures.
- At5b: for elementary X, Y, the pair is compatible iff every X' in \tilde X minus the common part \tilde X ∩ \tilde Y and every Y' in \tilde Y minus the common part satisfy X' |o| Y'. In other words, compatibility of elementary figures is controlled by the binary relation |o| on their non-shared strata.
- Plus four further axioms Mag1–Mag4 (stated elsewhere).

Scholie: two presentations are equivalent, i.e. they give equivalent groupoids of structures.
- (i) The 'magasin' (store) presentation: a set M with relations ≤, ≪, |o| and a family \mathcal F ⊂ \mathfrak F_M of subsets. It satisfies Mag1–Mag4 plus compatibility conditions linking ≤, ≪, |o|.
- (ii) The 'atlas' presentation: (\mathcal F, ≤, ≪, |o|) satisfying At1–At5 plus Mag1–Mag4.

The passage between them sends F ↦ \tilde F one way and takes the join-irreducibles the other way. Grothendieck comments that the store viewpoint is handier for stating and organising the basic axioms, while the atlas viewpoint is handier for computation and reasoning once the axiomatics is in place.

Modern reading: this is a Birkhoff-type representation of a bounded-complete poset whose completely join-irreducible ('prime') elements are join-dense. Compatibility is determined by a binary relation on primes, and an extra incidence relation ≪ is generated by primes. The next page develops a third, 'symmetric' point of view: an incidence relation between the two sets M and \mathcal F.
errors: At3 (⇐) is a genuine coherence axiom, not a consequence: pairwise compatibility of elementary pieces does not in general imply that \tilde F ∪ \tilde G is bounded. As an axiom it is fine, but it is exactly a 'coherence' hypothesis in the domain-theoretic sense.

At5b is stated for elementary X, Y. If X ≤ Y, the differences are X̃\X̃=∅ and Ỹ\X̃, so the condition holds vacuously, which is consistent. No contradiction is visible, but the intended meaning of |o| (presumably 'non-incident/disjoint position' of strata) is not defined on this page.
The Scholie's equivalence is asserted without proof. It is plausible and routine, given At2 (injectivity of F ↦ \tilde F) and the stability of \tilde{\mathcal F} under bounded unions.

ideas.what: Figures as a bounded-complete poset whose completely join-irreducible elements (elementary figures/strata) are join-dense and order-determining (At1–At2 with this page)
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff-type representation of prime-algebraic (bounded-complete) posets; join-irreducibles of a lattice of stratified sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (finite distributive lattices, 1937); Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (prime algebraic domains, 1981)

ideas.what: Compatibility (existence of join) determined by a binary relation on elementary pieces (At3, At5b)
ideas.modern_name: Coherence; binary conflict relation of a prime event structure

ideas.what: Equivalence between the 'magasin' presentation (set of elementary figures with relations and a family of subsets) and the 'atlas' presentation (poset of figures with axioms), as equivalent groupoids
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of categories between prime event structures and prime-algebraic coherent domains (Stone/Birkhoff-type duality)

ideas.what: Program of a combinatorial axiomatics of tame stratified 'figures' (analysis situs / tame topology)
ideas.modern_name: Tame topology / o-minimal geometry; combinatorial stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimality); Grothendieck's tame topology programme in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces tame topology, but not this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck's two equivalent presentations of stratified 'figures' (the store of elementary figures with ≤, ≪, |o| versus the atlas of figures with At1–At5) have the same shape as the theory of event structures and domains in computer science. It has a set of primes, a binary conflict/compatibility relation, and an equivalence with prime-algebraic coherent domains. That theory was developed independently around 1981–87 (Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel). The link between tame-topological stratifications and event-structure duality does not seem to have been drawn.
missed.quote: Les deux points de vue (i) (M, ≤, ≪, |o|, F ⊂ 𝔉_M) ... (ii) (F, ≤, ≪, |o|) axiomes At1–At5 ... sont équivalents, i.e. donnent des catégories-groupoïdes équivalentes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, posets of strata, entrance paths) could borrow the domain-theoretic duality machinery, and vice versa.

missed.claim: This is an unpublished axiomatic foundation for tame topology, formulated purely order-theoretically with an extra incidence relation ≪ and a 'non-incidence' relation |o| on strata. As far as known, it was not pursued in the tame-topology literature.
missed.quote: Le point de vue "magasin" est plus pratique ... Le point de vue "atlas" me semble par contre plus commode pour le pratique du calcul
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a point-free, combinatorial axiomatics of stratified figures, alternative to o-minimal structures, of possible interest for definable/stratified homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The order theory itself is routine (Birkhoff-type representation, coherence). The page is mainly interesting as unpublished evidence of Grothendieck's point-free axiomatics for tame figures, and for its unremarked parallel with Winskel's event-structure/domain duality.
transcription_corrections: The relation symbol written '\not\leq' throughout (Déf, At3, At5b) is not 'not ≤'. It is the compatibility symbol (a crossed ≍-type sign, listed as ≭ on the previous page), defined by: {F,G} bounded above.
'(NB ⇒ cas déjà connu [?])' reads more like '(NB ⇒ est déjà connu)'.
'Scholie Les deux plans [?] de [?]' should read 'Scholie Les deux points de vue'.
Under the brace in (i), the text likely reads 'conditions [de compatibilité] ≤, ≪, |o|'; in (ii), '(F, ≤, ≪, |o|) avec axiomes At1–At5'.
The page number at bottom left is '21' (the archive count says page 20); the next page is numbered 22.
